fuentes/historia-de-belgrano/titulo.texto: History of Belgrano and of Argentine Independence

fuentes/historia-de-belgrano/resumen.texto: A biography of Manuel Belgrano that became a history of the revolution and the war of independence in the Río de la Plata, based on documents from the General Archive and on private papers cited in notes and appendices. It was the first to publish part of Belgrano’s autobiography. Mitre argues that a nation with its own characteristics had already formed in colonial society, that the revolution of 1810 made it visible under the leadership of Buenos Aires and an enlightened minority, and that independence and liberal organization were its outcome. The work grew with each edition in response to its critics, and the author declared the fourth, of 1887, definitive.

fuentes/historia-de-belgrano/por_que_imp.texto: It is the founding work of Argentine documentary historiography and of the account taught as national history. José Carlos Chiaramonte challenged its thesis of a nation predating 1810, and revisionists challenged the secondary place it gives to the caudillos and the interior.

fuentes/historia-de-belgrano/leer.0.titu.texto: Fourth and definitive edition (1887), volume 1, on Internet Archive

fuentes/estudios-historicos-belgrano-y-g.texto: Historical Studies on the Argentine Revolution: Belgrano and Güemes

Book in which Mitre responded to two articles by Dalmacio Vélez Sarsfield, “Historical Rectifications: General Belgrano, General Güemes,” which objected to facts and judgments in the History of Belgrano. Mitre discusses the objections one by one and sets against each the documents on which he had relied.
It is the first of the controversies that accompanied the History of Belgrano, and it shows that Mitre’s account was contested from the start on the ground of documentary evidence.

fuentes/comprobaciones-historicas/soport.texto: Book in two volumes: Historical Verifications on the History of Belgrano (1881) and New Historical Verifications on Argentine History (1882)

fuentes/comprobaciones-historicas/resume.texto: Mitre’s response to the criticisms that Vicente Fidel López had made of the third edition of the History of Belgrano. Mitre maintains that every historical claim must rest on documents the reader can verify, and he faults López for reconstructing events, scenes, and dialogues from memory and tradition without proof. The second volume discusses other points in the history of the revolution with new documents.

fuentes/comprobaciones-historicas/por_qu.texto: It sets out Mitre’s documentary method and is one of the two halves of the Mitre-López controversy.

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/titulo.texto: History of San Martín and of South American Emancipation

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/soporte.texto: Book, first edition in three volumes (1887-1888) and corrected second edition (1890)

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/resumen.texto: History of José de San Martín’s campaign from the Río de la Plata to Chile and Peru, which Mitre presents as the expansion of the Río de la Plata revolution within South American emancipation. He used documents from Argentine and Chilean archives and San Martín’s own correspondence. He presents San Martín as a disinterested leader who put emancipation ahead of personal ambition, and thus explains his retirement after the Guayaquil meeting with Simón Bolívar.

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/por_que_i.texto: It fixed the image of San Martín as the supreme hero of independence, which liberals and revisionists later shared. His interpretation of Guayaquil and his contrast between San Martín and Bolívar were disputed by Venezuelan historians such as Vicente Lecuna.

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/leer.1.ti.texto: First edition (1887), volume 1, on Internet Archive

fuentes/historia-de-san-martin/leer.2.ti.texto: Abridged English translation (The Emancipation of South America, 1893) on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/historia-de-la-republica-argenti.texto: History of the Argentine Republic: Its Origin, Its Revolution, and Its Political Development

A narrative history in ten volumes that runs from the colonial origins to 1829, although the subtitle announced it would reach 1852. López writes a political narrative with portraits, scenes, and reconstructed speeches, and supports his version with documents, with the memories of his father, Vicente López y Planes, and with testimony from protagonists he knew. He argues that the historian must interpret the meaning of events and not limit himself to transcribing documents.

It was the great narrative alternative to Mitre’s work in the 19th century and was widely read as a textbook. Mitre, and later Rómulo Carbia and the Nueva Escuela Histórica, faulted it for claims without proof and for imagined reconstructions.

fuentes/debate-historico-lopez/titulo.texto: Historical Debate: Rebuttal of the Historical Verifications on the History of Belgrano

fuentes/debate-historico-lopez/resumen.texto: Vicente Fidel López’s response to Mitre’s Historical Verifications. López defends the value of tradition and of the testimony of protagonists when documents are missing, and the need for an overall interpretation. He faults Mitre for a meticulous erudition that does not explain the meaning of events.

fuentes/debate-historico-lopez/por_que_i.texto: Together with Mitre’s Historical Verifications, it forms the first public discussion of historical method in Argentina.

fuentes/revista-del-rio-de-la-plata/titu.texto: Revista del Río de la Plata: Monthly Journal of History and Literature of America

fuentes/revista-del-rio-de-la-plata/auto.texto: Andrés Lamas, Vicente Fidel López, and Juan María Gutiérrez

fuentes/revista-del-rio-de-la-plata/resu.texto: A journal edited in Buenos Aires by Andrés Lamas, Vicente Fidel López, and Juan María Gutiérrez, with studies of history, colonial and independence-era documents, and literary criticism. It published unpublished papers on the Río de la Plata and works by its editors.

fuentes/revista-del-rio-de-la-plata/por_.texto: It was the main organ of Río de la Plata historical studies before the Mitre-López controversy, and it shows the men of the Generation of 1837 at work as historians.

fuentes/revista-del-rio-de-la-plata/leer.texto: One volume from 1871 on Internet Archive

fuentes/historia-de-la-confederacion-arg.texto: History of the Argentine Confederation: Rozas and His Time
Book, first as History of Rozas and His Time (three volumes, 1881-1887), then corrected and expanded in five volumes (1892)

The first extensive history of the Rosas period, written with the governor’s own archive, which his daughter Manuela allowed him to consult in England. Saldías, a liberal who had fought against Mitre in the autonomist movement, condemns many aspects of Rosas’s government, but credits him with imposing order after the civil war and with defending sovereignty against the blockades by France and Great Britain.

Twentieth-century revisionists and Tulio Halperín Donghi (1970) placed it at the origin of historical revisionism. Mitre answered Saldías with a letter (1887) rejecting his judgment of Rosas, and twentieth-century revisionists cited that reply as proof that liberal history allowed no other version.

fuentes/la-epoca-de-rosas/titulo.texto: The Rosas Era: Its True Historical Character

fuentes/la-epoca-de-rosas/resumen.texto: An essay that explains Rosas as a product of his time and not as an individual anomaly. It compares the period after 1820 to an “Argentine Middle Ages” and Rosas to Louis XI of France, the king who subdued the feudal lords. Quesada drew on the archive of General Ángel Pacheco, the military chief of rosismo, which had passed to his family.

fuentes/la-epoca-de-rosas/por_que_import.texto: Along with Saldías’s work, it is one of the first attempts to explain rosismo without the condemnation of the 1840 exiles. The historian Pablo Buchbinder noted that, alongside his scientific interest, Quesada sought to rehabilitate Pacheco, a political relative of his.

fuentes/rosas-y-su-tiempo/resumen.texto: A study of Rosas’s government written by a positivist physician, who explains it through the psychology of the ruler and of the crowds that followed him, through the social setting of Buenos Aires, and through institutions such as the police, the Mazorca, the Church, and the press. It condemns the terror but treats it as a collective phenomenon and not only as the work of one individual.

fuentes/rosas-y-su-tiempo/por_que_import.texto: It continues Las multitudes argentinas (1899) by the same author and shows how the medical and sociological positivism of the early 20th century reread rosismo. Later historiography abandoned its psychopathological explanations.

fuentes/santiago-de-liniers-groussac/tit.texto: Santiago de Liniers, Count of Buenos Aires, 1753-1810

fuentes/santiago-de-liniers-groussac/res.texto: Biography of the French naval officer in Spanish service who led the reconquest of Buenos Aires during the first British invasion (1806), was viceroy of the Río de la Plata, and was executed by firing squad in 1810 on the orders of the First Junta, after leading the resistance in Córdoba. Groussac wrote it with a meticulous critique of the documents and earlier versions, and with a sympathetic judgment of the man, whom patriotic tradition remembered above all as an enemy of the revolution.

fuentes/santiago-de-liniers-groussac/por.texto: It is an example of Groussac’s critical method, which, from his post as director of the National Library, argued with several historians of his time.

fuentes/anales-de-la-biblioteca/soporte.texto: Publication of the National Library of Buenos Aires, ten volumes

fuentes/anales-de-la-biblioteca/resumen.texto: A National Library series directed by Groussac, which published colonial and independence-era documents held by the Library, with introductions and critical studies by him. It continued the journal La Biblioteca (1896-1898), also directed by him.

fuentes/anales-de-la-biblioteca/por_que_.texto: It put unpublished sources on the Río de la Plata into circulation and spread a model of critical document editing.

fuentes/estudio-sobre-las-guerras-civile.texto: Study on the Argentine Civil Wars

An essay that explains the civil wars of the 19th century by economic causes: the ruin of the interior’s production under commercial opening, the dispute over the Buenos Aires customs and river navigation, currency, and prices. Álvarez argues that the struggles between Unitarians and Federalists, or between caudillos, expressed regional conflicts of interest more than clashes of principle or temperament, and he proposes measures to keep them from recurring.
It was the first systematic economic interpretation of the civil wars, and it anticipated themes later taken up by Miron Burgin and José Carlos Chiaramonte.

fuentes/la-evolucion-de-las-ideas-argent.texto: Book in two volumes, La Revolución (1918) and La Restauración (1920), left unfinished

A history of ideas that reads the Argentine past as a clash between a colonial, feudal, and clerical mentality and a revolutionary, enlightened, and liberal one, each tied to social and economic interests. The May Revolution is the triumph of the second, and Rosas’s government is a restoration of colonial order supported by the estancieros, the Church, and the rural masses. Ingenieros died in 1925 without writing the volumes on the later period.
It was the most influential synthesis of Argentine positivism and reformist socialism on the 19th century, and it anticipated economic explanations that later authors took up.

fuentes/historia-critica-de-la-historiog.texto: Book, first as History of Argentine Historiography (1925) and later expanded

The first systematic history of Argentine historiography, from the colonial chroniclers to the historians of the early 20th century. Carbia classifies 19th-century authors into a “philosophist” school, which interpreted without sufficient documentary support, with Vicente Fidel López as its main figure, and an “erudite” or documentary school, headed by Mitre. He presents the Nueva Escuela Histórica, to which he belonged, as the continuation of the latter.
It fixed the classification by which the Mitre-López controversy is remembered. Written by a member of the Nueva Escuela, it also served as a genealogy of that school.

fuentes/la-representacion-de-los-hacenda.texto: The Representation of the Hacendados by Mariano Moreno: Its Lack of Influence on the Country’s Economic Life and on the Events of May 1810

A study that challenges the place historiography had given since Mitre to the Representation of the Hacendados, which Mariano Moreno wrote in 1809 in favor of trade with the British. Molinari argues, with documents from the viceroyalty, that the writing did not influence Viceroy Cisneros’s decision to allow that trade, nor the events of May 1810.
It is an early example of the method of the Nueva Escuela Histórica, which reviewed inherited historical claims against documents.

fuentes/ensayo-historico-sobre-la-revolu.texto: Historical Essay on the May Revolution and Mariano Moreno

A study of the political, legal, and economic aspects of the May Revolution and of Mariano Moreno’s actions, based on viceregal documents. Levene looks for the roots of the revolution in the economy of the Río de la Plata at the end of the 18th century, in colonial institutions, and in Enlightenment ideas.
It is one of the works with which the Nueva Escuela Histórica added economic and institutional history to the political account inherited from Mitre.

fuentes/asambleas-constituyentes-argenti.texto: Six-volume documentary compilation (seven volumes), published by the Instituto de Investigaciones Históricas of the Facultad de Filosofía y Letras

A compilation, ordered and annotated by Emilio Ravignani, of the minutes, session diaries, drafts, and documents of the Argentine constituent assemblies and congresses since the Assembly of the Year XIII, together with the constitutional texts and the pacts between provinces that organized the country politically. It gathers texts that were scattered across archives, newspapers, and official editions.
It is the main printed source for studying Argentina’s constitutional organization, and an example of the documentary work of the Nueva Escuela Histórica.

fuentes/historia-de-la-nacion-argentina-.texto: History of the Argentine Nation (from its origins to its definitive organization in 1862)
Collective work in ten volumes, published by the Junta de Historia y Numismática Americana, later the Academia Nacional de la Historia

A collective history directed by Ricardo Levene and published with state support, in which dozens of specialists wrote chapters on Indigenous peoples, the conquest, the colony, the revolution, the civil wars, and national organization up to 1862, with abundant quotations from documents. Its plan follows the traditional political periodization (colony, revolution, civil wars, and organization) and expands it with economic, institutional, and cultural history.
It was the synthesis of the academic historiography of its time. Revisionists called it the “official history” because of its state sponsorship and its continuity with Mitre.

fuentes/historia-argentina-dominguez/res.texto: A manual of Argentine history from the discovery to 1820, written by a porteño liberal who had been an exile during Rosas’s government. For decades it was the textbook of national history.

fuentes/historia-argentina-dominguez/por.texto: It is one of the first manuals of national history, predating the History of Belgrano in its definitive form.

fuentes/historia-argentina-dominguez/lee.texto: 1868 edition of the first part, up to 1807, on Internet Archive

fuentes/juan-facundo-quiroga-pena/soport.texto: Book based on lectures given in 1903 at the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of Buenos Aires

fuentes/juan-facundo-quiroga-pena/resume.texto: A study of the Riojan caudillo Facundo Quiroga, born from a series of lectures that the writer and playwright David Peña gave at the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of Buenos Aires. It challenges the portrait of Quiroga fixed by Sarmiento’s Facundo (1845), as a symbol of barbarism, backwardness, and cruelty, and it vindicates his figure.

fuentes/juan-facundo-quiroga-pena/por_qu.texto: Scholars of revisionism point to it as the first vindication of Quiroga and as a precedent for that current. It shows that the revision of the caudillos began in university circles in the early 20th century, before the nationalist revisionism of the 1930s.

fuentes/juan-manuel-de-rosas-ibarguren/t.texto: Juan Manuel de Rosas: His Life, His Time, His Drama

fuentes/juan-manuel-de-rosas-ibarguren/r.texto: A biography of Rosas written with documents and narrative resources, which presents him as a man of order who rose from the Buenos Aires countryside, capable of imposing authority after the anarchy, and which describes the repression as part of the drama of his time. It went through numerous editions and was a great popular success.

fuentes/juan-manuel-de-rosas-ibarguren/p.texto: It was the first widely circulated biography favorable to Rosas and paved the way for nationalist revisionism. It appeared in the year of José Félix Uriburu’s coup, which its author supported.

fuentes/la-argentina-y-el-imperialismo-b.texto: Argentina and British Imperialism: The Links of a Chain, 1806-1933

A book by Rodolfo and Julio Irazusta, written in response to the Roca-Runciman Pact of 1933 with Great Britain. It argues that since the British invasions a porteño oligarchy allied with British interests had subordinated the Argentine economy, and that liberal history concealed this dependence. Rosas appears as the ruler who resisted it.

It joined the defense of Rosas with the denunciation of British imperialism, a central axis of all later revisionism. Tulio Halperín Donghi (1970) saw in this turn of the 1930s the move of revisionism from a reappraisal of the Rosas period to a political interpretation of all national history.

fuentes/vida-politica-de-rosas/titulo.texto: Political Life of Juan Manuel de Rosas through His Correspondence

fuentes/vida-politica-de-rosas/soporte.texto: Book in several volumes, published from 1941

fuentes/vida-politica-de-rosas/resumen.texto: A political history of Rosas’s government built on his correspondence and that of his collaborators, extensively transcribed. Irazusta defends Rosas’s foreign policy toward France and Great Britain and his handling of relations with the provinces, and he explains the repression as a response to conspiracies and to civil war.

fuentes/vida-politica-de-rosas/por_que_i.texto: It is Julio Irazusta’s most extensive work and one of the most cited in revisionism. The main criticism, which applies to all revisionism, is that it uses government documents and justifies terror as political necessity. John Lynch (1981) reconstructed the same period with a different judgment of the repression.

fuentes/la-historia-falsificada/resumen.texto: A brief essay that accuses liberal historiography, from Mitre onward, of having written a partisan history that justified the victors of Caseros and Pavón and condemned the caudillos and Rosas. Palacio calls for reviewing that history from a nationalist and Catholic point of view.

fuentes/la-historia-falsificada/por_que_.texto: It is one of the manifestos of revisionism and spread the idea of a falsified “official history.” It is a programmatic text, not a documentary investigation.

fuentes/vida-de-don-juan-manuel-de-rosas.texto: Life of Don Juan Manuel de Rosas

A novelized biography of Rosas written by a nationalist novelist who was vice president of the Instituto Juan Manuel de Rosas. It presents Rosas as a defender of the nation and of Catholic order against the Unitarians and the European powers, with openly declared admiration.
It was one of the books that brought the revisionist image of Rosas to a broad public.

fuentes/politica-britanica-en-el-rio-de-.texto: British Policy in the Río de la Plata

An essay on British influence in Argentina since independence: the Baring Brothers loan of 1824, British mediation in Uruguay’s independence, the railways, and banking. Scalabrini Ortiz argues that British policy sought to keep the Río de la Plata divided and dependent, and that liberal history presented it as a friendship.
Together with his Historia de los ferrocarriles argentinos, it was one of the foundations of the anti-imperialism of FORJA and of Peronism.

fuentes/la-caida-de-rosas/resumen.texto: A study of the foreign policy of Rosas’s last years and of the alliance between the Empire of Brazil, Urquiza, and the Montevideo government that defeated him at Caseros. It was written during José María Rosa’s exile in Spain after 1955. Rosa interprets Caseros as a victory of Brazilian diplomacy and foreign interests rather than as a liberation.

fuentes/la-caida-de-rosas/por_que_import.texto: It is one of José María Rosa’s books on the diplomacy of the period. His reading of Caseros is the revisionist one, opposed to that of liberal historiography, which celebrated it as the end of tyranny.

fuentes/la-guerra-del-paraguay-y-las-mon.texto: The Paraguayan War and the Argentine Montoneras

A book that presents the War of the Triple Alliance as an aggression by Brazil and Mitre’s government against the Paraguay of Francisco Solano López, for the benefit of British interests. It links the war to the federal uprisings of the interior against it, such as that of Felipe Varela.
It spread the revisionist version of the war in Argentina, which Francisco Doratioto and Thomas Whigham later discussed with documents from the archives of the belligerent countries.

fuentes/politica-nacional-y-revisionismo.texto: An essay arguing that Argentine school history, the version written by Mitre, was a political instrument to justify a dependent agro-exporting country, and that revising it was a precondition of any national politics. Jauretche proposes reading the past according to its usefulness for the economic emancipation of the present.

It makes explicit the link between revisionism and Peronism after 1955. Tulio Halperín Donghi (1970) made this subordination of history to politics the main objection of academic historiography to revisionism.

fuentes/de-la-colonia-a-la-revolucion/re.texto: A Marxist essay on colonial society in the Río de la Plata and the origins of the 1810 revolution, written when Puiggrós was a member of the Communist Party. It interprets the colony as a society with feudal features and the revolution as the beginning of a bourgeois transformation.

fuentes/de-la-colonia-a-la-revolucion/po.texto: It opened the Marxist debate on the character of colonial society, in which Sergio Bagú (1949) and Milcíades Peña argued the opposite thesis: that a colonial economy was already oriented toward the world market.

fuentes/rosas-el-pequeno/resumen.texto: A Marxist essay against the nationalist vindication of Rosas, published in Montevideo, which presents the governor as a representative of the Buenos Aires estancieros and saladero owners and not as a defender of the nation.

fuentes/rosas-el-pequeno/por_que_importa.texto: It shows the position of the communist left of the 1940s against Rosista revisionism, which Puiggrós himself qualified later, when he moved closer to Peronism.

fuentes/revolucion-y-contrarrevolucion/r.texto: An Argentine history written from the “national left,” combining Marxist categories with revisionism. The May Revolution appears as part of a Spanish American revolution whose unity was thwarted by the Buenos Aires oligarchy and its alliance with Great Britain; the caudillos of the interior represent the masses and the nation, and Peronism continues that struggle. Ramos criticizes both liberal history and the traditional left, which he accuses of having accepted Mitre’s account.

fuentes/revolucion-y-contrarrevolucion/p.texto: It was the most widely read history book of the national left and brought revisionism to Marxist and Peronist readers. Milcíades Peña criticized it from a Marxist standpoint for idealizing the caudillos and for subordinating class analysis to the alliance with Peronism.

fuentes/historia-del-pueblo-argentino/so.texto: Written between 1955 and 1957 and published after the author's death in six volumes (1968-1973); collected in a single volume in 2012

fuentes/historia-del-pueblo-argentino/re.texto: A Marxist history that explains the Argentine past through class structure and the country's insertion into the world market. Peña argues that colonial society was already oriented toward the market and was not feudal; that Unitarians and Federalists were factions of the same class of landowners and merchants; that Rosas was the great estanciero of that class and not a defender of the people; and he condemns the Paraguayan War.

fuentes/historia-del-pueblo-argentino/po.texto: It argued at once with liberal history, with nationalist revisionism and with Jorge Abelardo Ramos’s national left, and was later cited by academic historians such as Tulio Halperín Donghi.

fuentes/la-guerra-del-paraguay-pomer/tit.texto: The Paraguayan War: A Great Business!

fuentes/la-guerra-del-paraguay-pomer/sop.texto: Book, reissued as The Paraguayan War: State, Politics and Business

fuentes/la-guerra-del-paraguay-pomer/res.texto: A study of the War of the Triple Alliance that highlights the profits of army suppliers and Buenos Aires merchants, the opposition to the war in the provinces and the resistance of conscripts. Pomer argues that the war served the Buenos Aires oligarchy, the Empire of Brazil and British capital against an autonomously developing Paraguay.

fuentes/la-guerra-del-paraguay-pomer/por.texto: It spread in the left and among revisionists the thesis of a war driven by British interests. Francisco Doratioto (2002) and Thomas Whigham (2002), using the archives of the belligerent countries, and Leslie Bethell (1996), using British papers, concluded that this thesis has no documentary support and explained the war by the conflicts among the states of the region.

fuentes/genocidio-americano/resumen.texto: A popular book by a Brazilian journalist that presents the war as a genocide planned by the Empire of Brazil and its allies, in the service of Great Britain, against an egalitarian and independent Paraguay, and gives very high figures for Paraguayan losses.

fuentes/genocidio-americano/por_que_impo.texto: It had wide circulation in Brazil during the military dictatorship and popularized the anti-imperialist thesis; Francisco Doratioto criticized it for the lack of documentary basis for its claims.

fuentes/maldita-guerra/titulo.texto: Damned War: A New History of the Paraguayan War

fuentes/maldita-guerra/resumen.texto: A general history of the War of the Triple Alliance based on archives in Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay and on British diplomatic documents. Doratioto explains the war by the rivalry among the states of the region over Uruguay and river navigation, by Brazilian intervention in Uruguay and by the calculations of Francisco Solano López, and finds no evidence that Great Britain promoted it.

fuentes/maldita-guerra/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the most cited academic syntheses of the war and one of the main refutations of the theses of León Pomer and Júlio José Chiavenato.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-whigham/titul.texto: The Paraguayan War, Volume 1: Causes and First Operations

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-whigham/resum.texto: The first volume of a history of the War of the Triple Alliance that studies its causes in the formation of the states of the Plata basin, in the disputes over borders and navigation and in the policy of Francisco Solano López, and narrates the first campaigns. Whigham uses Paraguayan, Brazilian, Argentine and British archives.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-whigham/por_q.texto: Together with Doratioto’s Maldita guerra, it is one of the main academic studies of the war; both explain the conflict by regional causes and not by a British plan.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-rosetta-stone/tit.texto: The Paraguayan Rosetta Stone: New Light on the Demography of the Paraguayan War, 1864-1870

fuentes/the-paraguayan-rosetta-stone/sop.texto: Article in Latin American Research Review, written with Barbara Potthast

fuentes/the-paraguayan-rosetta-stone/res.texto: An article by Thomas Whigham and Barbara Potthast that, based on a Paraguayan census of 1846 and on postwar counts, estimates the population of Paraguay before the war at between 420,000 and 450,000 inhabitants and its losses at between 60 and 69 percent.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-rosetta-stone/por.texto: It is one of the most cited academic estimates of Paraguayan losses and the direct answer to Vera Blinn Reber, who had proposed much smaller figures. Reber and Jan Kleinpenning discussed its method, and Whigham and Potthast replied to them in 2002.

fuentes/the-demographics-of-paraguay-reb.texto: The Demographics of Paraguay: A Reinterpretation of the Great War, 1864-1870
Article in Hispanic American Historical Review

An article that reviews Paraguayan demographic sources and argues that the population losses in the war, although grave, had been greatly exaggerated, and that much of the death toll was due to epidemics and hunger more than to combat.
It opened the academic debate over the war’s figures, which continued with the study by Whigham and Potthast (1999), with estimates far higher.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-bethell/sopor.texto: Research paper of the Institute of Latin American Studies of the University of London

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-bethell/resum.texto: An essay that examines the role of Great Britain in the War of the Triple Alliance using British diplomatic and financial documents. Bethell concludes that the British government remained neutral, did not promote the war, and that the loans from British banks to the allies were limited and did not determine it.

fuentes/the-paraguayan-war-bethell/por_q.texto: It is the most direct refutation, from British archives, of the thesis of a war provoked by British imperialism.

fuentes/las-ideas-politicas-en-argentina.texto: A synthesis of Argentine political history from the colony to 1945, through the ideas and social groups that sustained them. Romero distinguishes an authoritarian tradition rooted in the colony from a liberal one, describes the period of the caudillos as an “inorganic democracy” of rural masses, and calls the Argentina transformed by immigration since the late 19th century the “alluvial era.”
He treated both the liberal elite and the federal masses as actors in political history; categories such as “inorganic democracy” and “alluvial era” were taken up by later historiography.

fuentes/breve-historia-de-la-argentina/r.texto: A synthesis of Argentine history from the Indigenous population to the mid-20th century, written for the university publisher Eudeba, which organizes the account around the formation of society, from criollo to alluvial Argentina, rather than around battles and governments.

fuentes/breve-historia-de-la-argentina/p.texto: It went through many reprints and shows the social history that university renewal after 1955 set against both the liberal and the revisionist accounts.

fuentes/tradicion-politica-espanola-e-id.texto: Spanish Political Tradition and the Revolutionary Ideology of May

A study of the political ideas with which the May Revolution was made, which discusses the thesis of Manuel Giménez Fernández and Guillermo Furlong on the Suarezian roots of revolutionary thought. Halperín surveys the Spanish political tradition, from scholasticism to the Enlightenment and the crisis of the monarchy in 1808, and argues that no direct line can be drawn from Francisco Suárez to the arguments of 1810.
It is one of the main academic responses to the debate over the doctrinal origin of May.

fuentes/el-revisionismo-historico-argent.texto: A short essay that studies revisionism as a political and intellectual phenomenon, from Saldías and Quesada to the nationalist authors of the 1930s and their encounter with Peronism. Halperín argues that revisionism's success owed more to its political function, as a critique of the liberal order, than to new research, and that it never offered a complete alternative history.
It is one of the most cited analyses of revisionism from academic historiography.

fuentes/revolucion-y-guerra/titulo.texto: Revolution and War: The Formation of a Ruling Elite in Creole Argentina

fuentes/revolucion-y-guerra/resumen.texto: A study of how the revolution and the War of Independence transformed Río de la Plata society and its ruling elite between the late colonial period and the early 1820s. Halperín shows the weight of war in the militarization of politics, the emergence of a revolutionary career as a new path to advancement, the shift of the bases of power to the countryside and the breakup of the economic space of the viceroyalty, rather than a story of heroes or of a pre-existing nation.

fuentes/revolucion-y-guerra/por_que_impo.texto: It is one of the most cited works on independence in Argentine university historiography.

fuentes/una-nacion-para-el-desierto-arge.texto: A Nation for the Argentine Desert
Preliminary study to the anthology Project and Construction of a Nation (Caracas, 1980), published separately in 1982

An essay on the nation-building projects of Argentine intellectuals and politicians between 1846 and 1880, such as Alberdi, Sarmiento, Mitre and the men of the Confederation and of Buenos Aires, and on the distance between those projects and the state that was actually built until the federalization of Buenos Aires.
It studies the protagonists of national organization as authors of competing programs rather than as predestined founders, and it is one of the most widely read interpretations of the period.

fuentes/nacionalismo-y-liberalismo-econo.texto: Economic Nationalism and Liberalism in Argentina, 1860-1880

A study of the Argentine economic debates between 1860 and 1880, especially the discussions over the protection of industry in Congress and in the press during the crisis of the mid-1870s, in which Vicente Fidel López, Carlos Pellegrini and others defended protectionist tariffs. Chiaramonte shows that within the liberal elite there was a current of economic nationalism and that free trade was not a unanimous doctrine.
It challenges the image, shared by liberals and revisionists, of a 19th-century elite handed over without nuance to free trade.

fuentes/ciudades-provincias-estados/titu.texto: Cities, Provinces, States: Origins of the Argentine Nation (1800-1846)

fuentes/ciudades-provincias-estados/sopo.texto: Anthology of documents with an extensive preliminary study

fuentes/ciudades-provincias-estados/resu.texto: A study and selection of documents on the political organization of the Río de la Plata from the late colonial period to 1846. Chiaramonte argues that in 1810 there was no Argentine nation: the sovereign subjects were the cities and later the provinces, which acted as independent states linked by confederal pacts, and the idea of an earlier Argentine nationality was a later construction of Romanticism and of historiography.

fuentes/ciudades-provincias-estados/por_.texto: It is a systematic critique of Mitre’s thesis of a pre-existing nation, which revisionism also took for granted, and it changed the way the period of provincial autonomies is studied.

fuentes/aspectos-economicos-del-federali.texto: The Economic Aspects of Argentine Federalism
Book published by Harvard University Press, translated into Spanish in 1960

A study of the economic bases of the conflicts between Buenos Aires and the provinces from 1820 to 1852: the Buenos Aires customs house, tariffs, currency and public finances. Burgin shows that Buenos Aires kept control of customs revenue, analyzes Rosas’s 1835 customs law, which protected some interior production, and explains federalism as an expression of regional economic interests.
It was the first academic research on the economy of the Rosas period and remains a reference on the question of customs and river navigation.

fuentes/juan-manuel-de-rosas-lynch/resum.texto: A biography and study of the Rosas regime based on Argentine and British archives. Lynch describes the social base of Rosismo among the estancieros and urban and rural popular sectors, the cattle economy and foreign policy, and argues that terror, including the Mazorca, was a deliberate instrument of government controlled from above and not a spontaneous excess.

fuentes/juan-manuel-de-rosas-lynch/por_q.texto: It is one of the most cited academic biographies of Rosas, and it challenges both the moral condemnation of liberal history and the revisionist justification of repression. Jorge Myers later studied the republican discourse with which Rosismo legitimized itself, an aspect that the image of a personal dictatorship had left in the background.

fuentes/orden-y-virtud/titulo.texto: Order and Virtue: Republican Discourse under the Rosas Regime

fuentes/orden-y-virtud/resumen.texto: A study of the political language of Rosismo based on the official press, government messages and propaganda. Myers argues that the regime presented itself with a classical republican discourse, centered on order, the virtue of citizens and the defense of the republic against its internal and external enemies.

fuentes/orden-y-virtud/por_que_importa.texto: It shifted the discussion of Rosas from moral judgment to the way the regime legitimized itself before society.

fuentes/el-orden-conservador/titulo.texto: The Conservative Order: Argentine Politics between 1880 and 1916

fuentes/el-orden-conservador/resumen.texto: A study of the Argentine political regime between Julio A. Roca's first presidency and the rise of Hipólito Yrigoyen. Botana shows how the Partido Autonomista Nacional and the governors controlled the presidential succession under a Constitution that formally guaranteed suffrage, with low turnout and fraud, and how Roque Sáenz Peña's 1912 electoral reform tried to open that order.

fuentes/el-orden-conservador/por_que_imp.texto: It is the classic interpretation of the politics of the conservative republic; later studies, such as those of Hilda Sabato and Paula Alonso, qualified the image of a closed regime by showing electoral mobilization and competition among factions.

fuentes/la-formacion-del-estado-argentin.texto: The Formation of the Argentine State

A study of how the Argentine national state was built between Caseros and 1880: the conquest of the monopoly of force, the creation of a fiscal and administrative apparatus and the integration of the provinces. Oszlak distinguishes forms of state “penetration,” repressive, material, cooperative and ideological, through which the central government imposed itself on provincial powers.
It is one of the reference works on the formation of the state in Argentina and applies political science concepts to that process.

fuentes/economia-de-la-sociedad-colonial.texto: Economy of Colonial Society: An Essay in the Comparative History of Latin America

An essay in comparative economic history arguing that the Iberian colonies of America were not feudal societies but economies oriented from their origin toward the world market, with forms of forced labor in the service of production for export; Bagú describes them as a colonial capitalism.
It is one of the principal works of the thesis that challenged the feudal interpretation of the colony held by Rodolfo Puiggrós and other Marxist authors.

fuentes/las-doctrinas-populistas/titulo.texto: Populist Doctrines in the Independence of Spanish America

fuentes/las-doctrinas-populistas/resumen.texto: A study arguing that the revolutionaries of 1810 in Buenos Aires and in other American capitals founded the formation of juntas on the doctrine of Francisco Suárez and Spanish scholasticism on the popular origin of power: when the king was absent, sovereignty returned to the peoples. Giménez Fernández reads in this sense the arguments of the cabildo abierto of May 22 and denies that the main source was Rousseau.

fuentes/las-doctrinas-populistas/por_que.texto: It opened the debate between the Suarezian thesis, taken up by Guillermo Furlong, and the thesis of the influence of the Enlightenment and of Rousseau, held since Mitre; Tulio Halperín Donghi (1961) questioned whether that direct filiation could be proven.

fuentes/nacimiento-y-desarrollo-de-la-fi.texto: The Birth and Development of Philosophy in the Río de la Plata, 1536-1810

A history of the teaching of philosophy and of its authors in the colonial Río de la Plata, especially at the University of Córdoba and in the Jesuit colleges, based on manuscript course notes and theses. Furlong argues that scholasticism, and in particular Francisco Suárez's doctrine on the popular origin of power, shaped the generation of 1810 more than the authors of the French Enlightenment.

It is Furlong's principal work on the Suarezian thesis of the May Revolution and on the revaluation of Catholic colonial culture; the main objection, raised by Halperín Donghi, is that it does not follow from scholastic teaching that the revolutionaries acted according to that doctrine.

fuentes/la-conquista-del-desierto-walthe.texto: Book published by the Círculo Militar

A military history of the southern frontier, published by the Círculo Militar, which gathers reports, orders and memoirs of the campaigns against the Indigenous peoples of the pampas and Patagonia from the 16th century to 1885, culminating in Julio A. Roca's 1879 campaign. It presents the conquest as an enterprise of sovereignty and civilization.

For decades it was the reference history of the Conquest of the Desert and it conveys the point of view of the Army; Enrique Mases and Walter Delrio later studied what that version left out: the fate of the prisoners, the distribution of Indigenous families and the appropriation of their lands.

fuentes/estado-y-cuestion-indigena/titul.texto: State and the Indigenous Question: The Final Fate of the Subjugated Indians in the South of the Territory (1878-1910)

fuentes/estado-y-cuestion-indigena/resum.texto: A study, based on official documents, the press and archives, of what the Argentine state did with the subjugated Indigenous people after the campaigns of 1878-1885: their concentration in depots such as the Martín García island, the separation of families, their distribution as laborers, soldiers and domestic servants, and the projects of reductions and colonies.

fuentes/estado-y-cuestion-indigena/por_q.texto: It opened the academic study of the fate of the defeated in the Conquest of the Desert, which military historiography had left out.

fuentes/indios-ejercito-y-frontera/resum.texto: An essay written during its author's Mexican exile, which rereads the Conquest of the Desert and the campaigns against the Indigenous peoples through the texts of military men, travelers and 19th-century writers. Viñas argues that violence against Indigenous peoples was constitutive of the liberal state and relates it to the repression of the military dictatorship of 1976.

fuentes/indios-ejercito-y-frontera/por_q.texto: It was one of the first critical readings of the Conquest of the Desert from the intellectual left; its parallel with the dictatorship shows how that past was read from the political present.

personas/adolfo-saldias/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires lawyer who was active in Adolfo Alsina's autonomism, opposed to Mitre, and took part in the Revolución del Parque (1890). With the Rosas archive, which Manuela Rosas allowed him to consult in England, he wrote the Historia de Rozas y su época (1881-1887), later expanded as Historia de la Confederación Argentina (1892), the first extensive history of the period that did not start from the condemnation by the Unitarian exiles. He died in La Paz, Bolivia.

personas/ernesto-quesada/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires jurist, sociologist and historian, son of the writer and diplomat Vicente G. Quesada; as a child he visited Rosas in his exile near Southampton. In The Age of Rosas (1898) he explained the governor as a product of his time, using documents from the archive of General Ángel Pacheco. He held the chair of Sociology at the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of the University of Buenos Aires from 1904 to 1924.

personas/adolfo-carranza/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires lawyer and historian who proposed the creation of the Museo Histórico de la Capital (1889), nationalized in 1891 as the Museo Histórico Nacional, and directed it for twenty-five years, until his death. He gathered in it objects and documents from the independence and the civil wars that were scattered across state offices and private collections.

personas/ricardo-levene/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian, one of the figures of the Nueva Escuela Histórica, professor in La Plata and in Buenos Aires, and a scholar of the economic history of the viceroyalty and of the law of the Indies. He presided over the Junta de Historia y Numismática Americana, which in 1938 he renamed the Academia Nacional de la Historia, and directed the Historia de la Nación Argentina (1936-1950). In The Indies Were Not Colonies (1951) he argued that the American territories were kingdoms of the Crown and not colonies.

personas/emilio-ravignani/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian of the Nueva Escuela Histórica, who directed the historical research section of the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of the University of Buenos Aires from 1920 to 1946. The section became the Institute of Historical Research in 1921, and today bears his name. Under his direction the institute published document series, among them Argentine Constituent Assemblies (1937-1939). He was a national deputy for the Unión Cívica Radical.

personas/diego-luis-molinari/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian who trained from 1914 in the historical research section of the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters, together with Ravignani and Carbia. In The Hacendados' Representation of Mariano Moreno (1914) he argued that this writing had not influenced the opening of trade in 1809. He was an official of Hipólito Yrigoyen and a Radical senator (1928), later joined Peronism, and directed the Institute of Historical Research from 1946 to 1955.

personas/carlos-ibarguren/resumen.texto: A lawyer and politician from Salta, presidential candidate of the Partido Demócrata Progresista in 1922, who in the 1920s moved from liberalism to corporatist nationalism. His biography Juan Manuel de Rosas (1930) was the first favorable to the governor to enjoy wide circulation. After the 1930 coup he was federal intervenor in Córdoba.

personas/rodolfo-irazusta/resumen.texto: A nationalist journalist and politician from Gualeguaychú, influenced by Charles Maurras, who directed the newspaper La Nueva República (1927). With his brother Julio he wrote Argentina and British Imperialism (1934) and took part in founding the Instituto Juan Manuel de Rosas.

personas/julio-irazusta/resumen.texto: A nationalist writer from Gualeguaychú, the younger brother of Rodolfo Irazusta, with whom he wrote Argentina and British Imperialism (1934). His Political Life of Juan Manuel de Rosas through His Correspondence, published in several volumes from 1941, gathers and extensively comments on the correspondence of Rosas and his collaborators.

personas/ernesto-palacio/resumen.texto: A nationalist writer, editor in chief of La Nueva República (1927). His essay Falsified History (1939) accused liberal historiography of having written a party history, and it became one of the manifestos of revisionism. He was a Peronist national deputy (1946-1952) and published a History of Argentina, 1515-1938 (1954).

personas/jose-maria-rosa/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires lawyer and professor who founded an Institute of Federalist Studies in Santa Fe in 1938 and was one of the most widely read historians of Rosista revisionism. He presided over the Instituto Juan Manuel de Rosas several times, the first in 1951. He took part in General Valle's Peronist uprising (1956), went into exile, and wrote The Fall of Rosas (1958) and The Paraguayan War and the Argentine Montoneras; with him a part of Peronism adopted the revisionist view. In 1973 Perón appointed him ambassador to Paraguay.

personas/vicente-sierra/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires lawyer and historian of the second generation of revisionism, who stressed the role of the Catholic Church and of the Hispanic heritage in Argentine history. He adhered to Peronism and distanced himself from it during the conflict with the Church in 1954-1955. His main work is a History of Argentina in ten volumes, published between the late 1950s and 1972.

personas/guillermo-furlong/resumen.texto: A Jesuit born in Arroyo Seco (Santa Fe), author of an extensive body of work on Río de la Plata colonial culture, the missions and the Jesuits. In The Birth and Development of Philosophy in the Río de la Plata (1952) he argued that scholasticism, and especially Francisco Suárez, weighed more than Rousseau in the formation of the men of May.

personas/rodolfo-puiggros/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian and journalist who wrote from a Marxist perspective on the colony, the May Revolution and Rosas, first as a Communist militant and then, from the 1940s, close to Peronism. He was rector of the University of Buenos Aires in 1973 and died in exile in Havana.

personas/jorge-abelardo-ramos/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires politician and writer of Trotskyist origin who founded the current of the “national left,” favorable to Peronism. In Revolution and Counterrevolution in Argentina (1957) he combined revisionism with Marxist categories. He was Carlos Menem's ambassador to Mexico from 1989.

personas/milciades-pena/resumen.texto: A Marxist historian and sociologist born in La Plata, with a Trotskyist background, who argued at once with liberal history, with nationalist revisionism and with Jorge Abelardo Ramos's national left. His History of the Argentine People, written between 1955 and 1957, was published after his death, at the age of 32, in six volumes (1968-1973).

personas/leon-pomer/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires lawyer and historian who researched the War of the Triple Alliance in the General Archive of the Nation and in the archive of the Museo Mitre. His book The Paraguayan War (1968) spread among the left and among revisionists the thesis of a war in the service of the Buenos Aires oligarchy, Brazil and British capital. Exiled in Brazil during the 1976 dictatorship, he taught at universities in São Paulo and Campinas; he died in Asunción.

personas/jose-luis-romero/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian, medievalist and scholar of social and intellectual history, one of the figures in the renewal of university history after 1955: he was interventor rector of the University of Buenos Aires in 1955 and dean of its Faculty of Philosophy and Letters in 1962. He wrote Political Ideas in Argentina (1946) and A Brief History of Argentina (1965).

personas/tulio-halperin-donghi/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires historian, a disciple of José Luis Romero, who left the Argentine university in 1966 and from 1972 taught at the University of California, Berkeley. He studied the 19th-century Río de la Plata in Revolution and War (1972) and in other books on elites, ideas and the state, and analyzed revisionism as a political and intellectual phenomenon (1970).

personas/jose-carlos-chiaramonte/resumen.texto: A historian born in Arroyo Seco (Santa Fe), director of the Ravignani Institute of the University of Buenos Aires from 1986 to 2012. He studied 19th-century Argentine economic thought and challenged the thesis of an Argentine nation prior to 1810: he argued that in the first half of the century the sovereign subjects were the cities and the provinces.

personas/john-lynch/resumen.texto: A British historian of Spain and of Spanish America, professor at the University of London and director of its Institute of Latin American Studies. His Argentine Dictator: Juan Manuel de Rosas (1981) is one of the most cited academic biographies of Rosas; he also wrote on the independence revolutions and on San Martín.

personas/francisco-doratioto/resumen.texto: A Brazilian historian, professor at the University of Brasília and a specialist in Brazil's relations with the countries of the Río de la Plata. His Damned War (2002), based on archives of the belligerent countries, is one of the most cited academic histories of the War of the Triple Alliance.

personas/thomas-whigham/resumen.texto: An American historian, professor at the University of Georgia and a specialist in 19th-century Paraguay. He wrote The Paraguayan War (2002), on the causes and beginning of the War of the Triple Alliance, and, with Barbara Potthast, an estimate of Paraguayan population losses (1999).

personas/leslie-bethell/resumen.texto: A British historian of Brazil and Latin America, professor at the University of London and editor of the Cambridge History of Latin America. In a 1996 study he examined, using British documents, the role of Great Britain in the Paraguayan War.

personas/juan-alvarez/resumen.texto: A lawyer, judge and historian born in Gualeguaychú and based in Rosario, who served as Attorney General of the Nation from 1935 to 1947. In Study on the Argentine Civil Wars (1914) he explained the conflicts of the 19th century by economic causes. In October 1945 President Edelmiro J. Farrell asked him to form a cabinet, which never took office.

personas/manuel-gimenez-fernandez/resume.texto: A Sevillian professor of canon law, Minister of Agriculture of the Second Republic for the CEDA, and later a Christian Democrat opponent of Francoism. A historian of Bartolomé de las Casas and of the law of the Indies, in Populist Doctrines in the Independence of Spanish America (1947) he argued that the American juntas of 1810 were founded on the doctrine of Francisco Suárez.

personas/natalio-botana/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires political scientist and historian. In The Conservative Order (1977) he studied the Argentine political regime from 1880 to 1916 and the electoral reform of Roque Sáenz Peña; he presided over the Academia Nacional de la Historia from 2021 to 2023.

personas/oscar-oszlak/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires political scientist who studies the state and public administration in Latin America. In The Formation of the Argentine State (1982) he analyzed how the national government imposed itself on the provincial powers between 1852 and 1880.

personas/david-vinas/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires novelist and critic who reread Argentine literature in relation to political violence. In his Mexican exile he wrote Indians, Army and Frontier (1982), a critical reading of the Conquest of the Desert.

personas/luis-l-dominguez/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires poet, politician and diplomat, who went into exile in Montevideo during Rosas's government. His Historia argentina (1861), which reached up to 1820, was for a long time the textbook for teaching national history; he died in London, where he was minister plenipotentiary.

personas/pacho-odonnell/resumen.texto: A Buenos Aires psychiatrist, writer and politician, author of popular history books from a revisionist standpoint. He presided over the Instituto Nacional de Revisionismo Histórico Manuel Dorrego from its creation in 2011 until his resignation at the beginning of 2014.

hechos/fundacion-del-archivo-general-de-.texto: On August 28, 1821, during Martín Rodríguez's government in Buenos Aires, the General Archive of the Province was created to gather the papers of the viceroyalty, of the revolutionary governments and of the provincial administration. In 1884 it passed to the Nation under the name General Archive of the Nation. Its holdings served as the basis for Mitre, who worked in it on his History of Belgrano, and for later historiography.

hechos/polemica-mitre-velez-sarsfield/ti.texto: Controversy between Mitre and Vélez Sarsfield over Belgrano and Güemes

hechos/polemica-mitre-velez-sarsfield/re.texto: In 1864 Dalmacio Vélez Sarsfield published two articles titled “Historical Rectifications: General Belgrano, General Güemes,” with objections to facts and judgments in the History of Belgrano. Mitre, then president of the Republic, replied the same year with a book that discussed each objection with documents. It was the first of the controversies that accompanied the successive editions of the work.

hechos/polemica-mitre-lopez/titulo.texto: Controversy between Mitre and Vicente Fidel López

hechos/polemica-mitre-lopez/resumen.texto: Between 1881 and 1882 Bartolomé Mitre and Vicente Fidel López argued in the press and in books over the History of Belgrano and over how history should be written: Mitre published the Historical Verifications (1881) and the New Verifications (1882), and López replied with the Historical Debate (1882). Mitre demanded that every claim be proven with documents and accused López of reconstructing facts and dialogues without evidence; López defended the value of tradition, of the testimony of the protagonists and of an overall interpretation. Rómulo Carbia (1925) described it as the clash between a “scholarly” school and a “philosophizing” one, and with that scheme the Nueva Escuela Histórica presented itself as the heir of Mitre's method.

hechos/fundacion-del-museo-historico-nac.texto: Founding of the Museo Histórico Nacional

On May 24, 1889, the mayor of Buenos Aires, Francisco Seeber, created the Museo Histórico de la Capital and appointed as director Adolfo P. Carranza, who had proposed it. It opened to the public in 1890, was nationalized by a decree of President Carlos Pellegrini of September 26, 1891, and since 1897 has operated in the Lezama mansion.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-junta-de-historia.texto: Founding of the Junta de Numismática Americana

In 1893 a group of collectors and scholars gathered by Bartolomé Mitre, among them Alejandro Rosa, founded the Junta de Numismática Americana in Buenos Aires. It came to be called the Junta de Historia y Numismática Americana, and Mitre presided over it until his death in 1906. In 1938, under the presidency of Ricardo Levene, it became the Academia Nacional de la Historia. Revisionists regarded it as the guardian of “official history.”

hechos/polemica-sobre-el-plan-de-operaci.texto: Controversy over the Authenticity of the Plan de operaciones

In 1896 Norberto Piñero included in the Writings of Mariano Moreno the Plan de operaciones attributed to Moreno, based on a copy kept in Spain. Paul Groussac declared it apocryphal and argued with Ernesto Quesada and with Piñero, who replied to him in 1897, and the discussion of its authorship continued throughout the 20th century. In his book A Bicentennial Plagiarism (2015), Diego Bauso showed that parts of the text copy passages from the French novel The Cemetery of the Magdalena, by Regnault-Warin, published from 1800 on, a finding that weighs against Moreno's authorship.

hechos/fundacion-del-museo-mitre/resumen.texto: After Bartolomé Mitre's death in January 1906, a law authorized the Executive to buy the house in which he had lived, on San Martín Street in Buenos Aires, to turn it into a museum, which opened to the public on June 3, 1907. It holds his library and archive, and it published the Documents of the San Martín Archive (1910-1911).

hechos/creacion-del-instituto-de-investi.texto: Creation of the Institute of Historical Research of the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters

In 1905 the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of Buenos Aires created a section of historical research, which from 1912 had Luis María Torres as director and Emilio Ravignani as head of research; in 1914 Rómulo Carbia and Diego Luis Molinari joined. In December 1921, with Ravignani as director since 1920, the section became the Institute of Historical Research, one of the centers of the Nueva Escuela Histórica, which published large series of documents.

hechos/fundacion-del-instituto-rosas/tit.texto: Founding of the Juan Manuel de Rosas Institute

hechos/fundacion-del-instituto-rosas/res.texto: In 1938 a group of nationalist writers, among them Manuel Gálvez, Roberto de Laferrère, Carlos Ibarguren, Ernesto Palacio and Rodolfo and Julio Irazusta, founded in Buenos Aires the Instituto de Investigaciones Históricas Juan Manuel de Rosas, which published a journal and became the center of Rosista revisionism. It set out to revise the history written by the victors of Caseros and to vindicate Rosas as a defender of sovereignty against France and Great Britain. Tulio Halperín Donghi (1970) studied it as an expression of the anti-liberal nationalism of the 1930s, which read the past according to the political struggles of the present; from the 1950s a part of its members, such as José María Rosa, identified with Peronism.

hechos/repatriacion-de-los-restos-de-ros.texto: Rosas died in exile in 1877 and was buried in Southampton; from 1934 there were commissions asking for his remains to be brought back, without result for decades. President Carlos Menem promoted the repatriation as a gesture of “national reconciliation”: on September 30, 1989 there was an event in Rosario, where Menem spoke, and a procession with descendants of Rosas and of his enemies, and the remains were buried in the Recoleta Cemetery. Menem presented the repatriation as part of the “national reconciliation,” the same slogan with which he justified the pardons of October 1989.

hechos/instituto-dorrego/titulo.texto: Instituto Nacional de Revisionismo Histórico Manuel Dorrego

hechos/instituto-dorrego/resumen.texto: Decree 1880/2011 of President Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, dated November 17, 2011, created the Instituto Nacional de Revisionismo Histórico Argentino e Iberoamericano Manuel Dorrego, first presided over by Pacho O'Donnell, to study and disseminate the figures vindicated by revisionism. University historians such as Hilda Sabato, Mirta Lobato, Juan Suriano and Luis Alberto Romero criticized it because it had the state promote an interpretation of history; its president rejected those criticisms. President Mauricio Macri dissolved it at the end of 2015 by Decree 269, published in the Boletín Oficial on January 4, 2016.

hechos/dia-de-la-soberania-nacional/titu.texto: Establishment of the Day of National Sovereignty

hechos/dia-de-la-soberania-nacional/resu.texto: In 1974, on the proposal of the historian José María Rosa, Congress established November 20, the anniversary of the battle of Vuelta de Obligado (1845), as the Day of National Sovereignty, promulgated by President María Estela Martínez de Perón. On November 3, 2010 Cristina Fernández de Kirchner made it a national holiday by a decree of necessity and urgency. The date enshrines the revisionist reading of Obligado as a defense of sovereignty; the historian Luis Alberto Romero objected that what the government of Rosas then defended was the commercial monopoly of the port of Buenos Aires against the provinces, more than a national cause.

lugares/archivo-general-de-la-nacion/res.texto: The largest archive in Argentina, created in 1821 as the archive of the Province of Buenos Aires and national since 1884. It holds the papers of the viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, of the revolutionary governments, of the Confederation and of the national state, which were the documentary basis of nearly all Argentine historiography. Since 2020 it has operated in a new building in Parque Patricios.

lugares/museo-historico-nacional/resumen.texto: A museum of Argentine history created in 1889 as the Museo Histórico de la Capital and national since 1891, operating since 1897 in the former Lezama mansion, facing Parque Lezama, in San Telmo. It holds objects from the independence, the civil wars and the national organization.

lugares/museo-mitre/resumen.texto: A colonial house on San Martín Street in Buenos Aires, where Bartolomé Mitre lived, converted into a museum in 1907, a year after his death. It holds his American library, his archive and the San Martín papers published in 1910 and 1911.

lugares/academia-nacional-de-la-historia.texto: A corporation of historians founded in 1893 as the Junta de Numismática Americana, later called the Junta de Historia y Numismática Americana, which took its current name in 1938. Between 1918 and 1971 it operated in the Museo Mitre, and since then it has had its seat in the preserved meeting hall of the former National Congress, beside Plaza de Mayo.

lugares/instituto-ravignani/resumen.texto: A history institute of the Faculty of Philosophy and Letters of the University of Buenos Aires, born in 1905 as a section of historical research, became the Institute of Historical Research in 1921, and after his death was named for Emilio Ravignani, its director from 1920 to 1946. It published large collections of documents and was a center of the Nueva Escuela Histórica and, later, of academic historiography.
